clue.text: Of hypothetical power in a parent — just a bit

indicators.note: the power word sits inside the parent word, so 'in' signals one piece placed within another

parts.note: mum is a mother, a parent
odic means relating to od, a hypothetical natural force proposed by the chemist Reichenbach

explanation.surface: A tiny dose of imagined power is handed to a mother or father.
explanation.walkthrough: Od was a life force proposed by Baron von Reichenbach in the 1840s, never shown to exist, hence 'hypothetical'; 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A small token amount is only a little piece of something.

clue.text: Just too few chairs for the show?

definitions.text: Just too few chairs for the show?

parts.words: Just too few chairs for the show?
parts.note: the party game with one chair too few for the players is named after music; the word also means a stage show with songs

explanation.surface: A theatre short of seating for its audience.
explanation.walkthrough: Musical chairs is the party game in which there is always one chair fewer than players.
explanation.definitionFit: A song-and-dance stage show shares its name with the first word of the game with too few chairs.

clue.text: Find no game and nothing in game

definitions.meaning: in hunting, to fail to find any quarry
a goalless tied game is a nil-all result

explanation.surface: A fruitless day of hunting and a scoreless match.
explanation.walkthrough: Draw blank is a fox-hunting phrase for finding no fox in a covert.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunt that finds no fox has failed, and a goalless tie gives a match with nothing on the scoreboard.

clue.text: Beast whose pelt I wear

parts.note: a coat is an animal's fur or pelt

explanation.surface: A fur-wearer boasting of the animal skin they have on.
explanation.definitionFit: This raccoon-like South American mammal is a wild animal.

clue.text: Paris place rather crumby ?

definitions.meaning: the famous church and square near the Paris boulevards
a small shell-shaped sponge cake that leaves crumbs

explanation.surface: Somewhere in Paris that is a bit shabby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumby' looks like 'crummy', meaning shabby, but it means full of crumbs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paris church of La Madeleine shares its name with the little sponge cake made famous by Proust.

clue.text: Worn by Falstaff's " two " assailants near Gadshill-—two beastly

definitions.text: Worn by Falstaff's " two " assailants near Gadshill

parts.note: a buck is a male deer, one beast
a ram is a male sheep, the second beast

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean robbery scene, with a parting jab at two brutish people.
explanation.walkthrough: In Henry IV Part 1 Falstaff boasts of fighting off 'two rogues in buckram suits' at Gadshill, a number that grows each time he tells it; buckram is a stiff cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Falstaff's imaginary attackers wore suits of this stiffened coarse cloth, in Shakespeare's comic tale.

clue.text: That strong-looking French tea is something to be borne

parts.note: brun is French for brown, the colour of strong tea
T is short for tea

explanation.surface: A dark French brew that must simply be endured.
explanation.definitionFit: The main force of a blow or burden is what one has to bear.

clue.text: Dancer of the "Pigeons"

definitions.meaning: the sweetheart of Harlequin, a dancing figure in pantomime
a word meaning dovelike, from Latin columba, a dove or pigeon

explanation.surface: A ballerina from a troupe called the Pigeons.
explanation.definitionFit: Harlequin's dancing partner in the harlequinade shares her name with an adjective for doves, from Latin columba.

clue.text: We don't deplore these of colour in our borders

definitions.text: We don't deplore these of colour in our borders

parts.words: We don't deplore these of colour in our borders
parts.note: flower borders bursting with colour are said to be a blaze of brightness; ordinarily such public disorder would be deplored

explanation.surface: A gardener happy about wild bursts of colour along the beds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders' looks like national frontiers, where unrest would be deplored, but means flower beds.
explanation.definitionFit: Disturbances are usually deplored, but a vivid show of flowers is praised by that phrase.

clue.text: Mouse-smacking steed

parts.note: mus is Latin for mouse
tang is a smack or sharp flavour, smacking of something

explanation.surface: A horse that swats at a mouse.
explanation.definitionFit: This feral horse of the American plains is a riding mount.

clue.text: House of South Carolina in the Milanese style

parts.note: SC is the abbreviation for the US state of South Carolina
à la means in the style of, as in the French cookery term à la milanaise

explanation.surface: A Southern US mansion built to look like something from Milan.
explanation.walkthrough: La Scala is Milan's famous opera house, so 'Milanese' points at the answer as well as giving the à la phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: La Scala is the celebrated opera house in Milan; house here means theatre.

clue.text: The French miss out from two crazy divers for Spanish gold

indicators.note: the French article is dropped out of the longer phrase, so 'miss out from' signals removal

parts.note: double means twofold, two of something
le is French for 'the'
loons are diving birds, and loon also means a crazy person

explanation.surface: Some unhinged swimmers missing out on Spanish treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: DOUBLE LOONS loses the LE in its middle, leaving the coin name.
explanation.definitionFit: These were old Spanish coins struck in gold, the treasure of pirate stories.

clue.text: Goat-leaping car

parts.note: the word for a light carriage or open-top car comes from a French word for a goat-like caper or leap

explanation.surface: A motor that bounds along like a goat.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabriole is a capering leap, from Italian capra 'goat', and the bouncy one-horse carriage named after it gave its name to convertible cars.

clue.text: Permafrost where he is ?

parts.note: alludes to Stephen Foster's song about a master lying 'in de cold, cold ground', and permafrost is ground that stays frozen

explanation.surface: Wondering about someone stranded in frozen Arctic ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Foster's minstrel song is called Massa's in de Cold Ground; the dialect word means master.
explanation.definitionFit: The dialect form of 'master' is the figure the song puts in cold ground, which the clue turns into permafrost.

clue.text: Re this, unchain or let on

definitions.meaning: putting RE before this word makes a word meaning unchain or set free
to let something on terms is to rent it out to a tenant

explanation.surface: Instructions about freeing something or renting it out.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is cryptic: RE plus the answer gives RELEASE, meaning unchain.
explanation.definitionFit: Renting property out by contract is to let it; adding RE makes the verb for freeing or unchaining.

clue.text: Make one fence fit for service

indicators.note: to make something is to fashion it from raw materials, so these letters are formed into a new word

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Instructions to build a fence that is serviceable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' looks like part of the definition, but it is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something working well and without waste is serviceable.

clue.text: Like the afflatus in topping off a church ?

parts.note: spiring means fitting a church with its steeple, the spire that tops it off

explanation.surface: Divine inspiration compared to crowning a church with something.
explanation.walkthrough: Afflatus is a divine creative impulse, a word solvers may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: Afflatus is a divine creative breath, the kind of influence that stirs and uplifts the mind.

clue.text: Is hoisted with joy, the red or green aboard

indicators.note: in a down clue a word hoisted is lifted upward, so read backwards

parts.note: delight means joy

explanation.surface: Joyfully raising the coloured lamps on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: A ship carries a red light on the port side and a green one to starboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's navigation lamps on either side are red to port and green to starboard.

clue.text: It's the turn of 12 to export it

definitions.text: It's the turn of 12 to export it

parts.words: It's the turn of 12 to export it
parts.note: 12 across turned round names an Indian state famous for exporting a beverage

explanation.surface: Someone's turn to send goods abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Reverse the 12 across answer to get ASSAM, the north-east Indian state whose tea is exported worldwide.
explanation.definitionFit: Assam produces and exports a strong black brew grown in India.

clue.text: Vicariously alert non-batting side.

parts.note: to be awake is to be alert; wake is a form of that word
in cricket the field is the team bowling and fielding, not batting

explanation.surface: A cricket team watching carefully while not batting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vicariously' is a pun on The Vicar of Wakefield, Oliver Goldsmith's novel; Wakefield is also a Yorkshire town.
explanation.definitionFit: The town is famous through Goldsmith's novel about its vicar, so 'Vicariously' hints at it.

clue.text: Irish creature

parts.note: the creature, or crathur, is Irish slang for strong liquor

explanation.surface: An animal from Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The Irish spelling has an E, unlike Scotch whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish call their distilled spirit 'the cratur', meaning creature.

clue.text: Latterly befriended, but that's past

indicators.note: latterly means at the latter end, so the letters come from the end of the next word

explanation.surface: A friendship made recently that is already over.
explanation.definitionFit: Something finished is over and done, in the past.

clue.text: An adder, Ed, might be

indicators.note: the letters might be rearranged into a different word, so 'might be' signals an anagram

explanation.surface: Telling someone named Ed that a viper could be feared.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a venomous snake is feared.
explanation.definitionFit: A venomous snake is feared by many.

clue.text: A sacrificial ram in place of this kid

definitions.text: A sacrificial ram in place of this kid

parts.words: A sacrificial ram in place of this kid
parts.note: in Genesis, Abraham sacrifices a ram caught in a thicket instead of his son

explanation.surface: A Bible story of a ram substituted for a child at the altar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kid' looks like a young goat to match the ram, but it means a child.
explanation.definitionFit: Abraham's son was spared when God provided a ram for the sacrifice in his place.

clue.text: Can't I do the twist ? What a caper!

indicators.note: the twist is a dance, and twisting the letters rearranges them

explanation.surface: Someone longing to dance the twist and enjoying the fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotesque or playful act is a caper.

clue.text: Where the chief dined — on turkey ?

parts.note: a sultan is the chief ruler of a Muslim state
ate means dined

explanation.surface: Asking where the boss had his meal, perhaps a turkey dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: The sultan of Turkey ruled the Ottoman Empire, so 'on turkey' is a pun: the bird's meal, and the realm.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultan's domain is the place he rules, so it answers 'where' for the chief.

clue.text: Shoot many in old Jerusalem

indicators.note: the letter for many goes inside the old name, so 'in' signals containment

parts.note: Sion is an old spelling of Zion, the hill of Jerusalem
C is the Roman numeral for 100, many

explanation.surface: Lots of people gunned down in ancient Jerusalem.
explanation.definitionFit: A young shoot or cutting used in grafting is also a word for an heir.

clue.text: Once more a good stroke of business?

parts.note: a gain is a profit, a good stroke of business

explanation.surface: Wanting another profitable deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something one more time is to repeat it.

clue.text: In. Northants a rebel straying without a right

parts.note: Robert Kett led a rebellion in Norfolk in 1549

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter for right is taken out

parts.note: erring means straying from the right path
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A wandering rebel somewhere in Northamptonshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Northants is Northamptonshire, an English Midlands county; Kett's Rebellion was a Tudor peasant revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: The town is in Northamptonshire, the county abbreviated Northants.

clue.text: Bill and Eddie in stage duo.?

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
Ted and Eddie are both pet forms of Edward

explanation.surface: Two named men performing together as a double act.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: what a pair of performers on stage did.
explanation.definitionFit: Performing in a stage double act means having performed a role.

clue.text: No reversion about a top cat in America

indicators.note: the reversed refusal goes about the other letters, so 'about' signals one piece surrounding another
reversion means turning back, so the word for no is read backwards

parts.note: nay means no
U is upper-class, the top of society
taken as written

explanation.surface: Declining to return to a superior feline living in the Americas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversion' turns the refusal backwards and 'about' wraps it round the top cat; Yucatán is in Mexico, so 'America' means the continent, not the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: The peninsula is in Mexico, part of the American continent.

clue.text: Where Man disposes

parts.note: plays on 'Man proposes, God disposes', with Man being the Isle of Man, whose parliament makes decisions

explanation.surface: A twist on the proverb that man proposes and God disposes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is a self-governing island in the Irish Sea with its own parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The Manx parliament is the place where the island's laws are settled.
